task.title: Find why a shared remote can end with a task ref pointing at a missing commit
task.description:
Found in review of PR #216 (2026-11-21). Reproduces on main, so it is not caused by that change.

Setup: two boards in worktrees of one repository, a sync watcher, and a second clone, all pushing to one temporary bare remote at once. Result: the bare remote was left with a task ref whose commit was missing (`fatal: missing object 2402e092… for refs/workbook/tasks/WB-…`), and `workbook sync` then exited 1. On main the same happened with a different object.

Likely cause, not confirmed: Git's own automatic gc running in the remote while pushes were landing (it left cruft packs, a multi-pack-index and commit-graphs). The reviewer's scripts were `syncwt.sh` and `flood.py` in its scratchpad, which may be gone; the setup above is enough to rebuild them.

Also seen, existing behavior: each `workbook rebuild` killed with -9 leaves a temporary cache file behind (51 after 150 kills) and nothing cleans them up.

## Done when
- The cause is known, with a reproduction that does not depend on luck.
- Either Workbook no longer triggers it, or the docs say what a team hosting its own bare remote must configure (for example gc settings), and what to do when it has happened.
- Leftover temporary cache files are removed by a later command.
